Ruled by the run owner 2026-08-09.** over Publishing a weaker bound under MATRIX §4's shortfall clause, or widening the corpus to more repos to reach T ~= 50 because The shortfall clause cannot actually be exercised: TRAP-SPEC §2.8 caps any single trap at 10% of the primary denominator, which needs >= 10 distinct traps before a pool is even valid, and there are 5 of which 4 are algrowth — so publishing would mean publishing a number the frozen spec forbids, at a ~18% upper bound consistent with a 1-in-6 failure rate. Widening the corpus fights a law rather than a shortage: measured end-to-end attrition is 592 -> 471 -> 122 -> 57 -> 20 authored -> 5 surviving = 0.8%, so 45 traps would need ~5,600 candidate decisions against the 592 five repos produced, and the attrition is M3's law (a well-kept record embodies its own decisions in code), which more repos only re-sample. The binding constraint is structural: trap-based design ties n to naturally-occurring historical decisions surviving five screens, a quantity that is ~1% of a record and cannot be grown on demand. Authored constraints satisfy the leak and embodiment screens BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by luck, and the temptation floor (k=4, 2-of-4) still gates entry to the denominator, so an authored constraint that does not actually tempt is excluded exactly as a historical one would be — which is what keeps authoring honest. The cost is external validity and it is accepted and must be stated in every report: the claim becomes "on planted constraints in real repos", not "on decisions this team actually made", which is what TRAP-SPEC §2.1's derive-from-real-records rule was protecting. The machinery is unaffected — cells, seals, isolation, runner, grading and all four screens work on authored constraints unchanged; only the corpus is replaced.
- 2026-08-10T08:01:27.088Z — rule: **Gate every scenario-4 constraint — authored set and historical anchor alike — at k=6 P cells with a 4-of-6 temptation floor; never admit one on 4 cells or on a 2-of-4 majority.** — chose **Tighten the scenario-4 temptation floor to k=6 P cells with a 4-of-6 gate (67% threshold), applied identically to the authored set and the 5-constraint historical anchor. Ruled by the run owner 2026-08-10.** over Carrying scenario 3's k=4 / 2-of-4 gate over unchanged; tightening the threshold only (3-of-4, same 4 cells); or going to 5-of-8. because The two gate errors are not symmetric. False ADMISSION of a weak-temptation constraint is non-conservative: its R-cell sessions are sprung by TRAP-SPEC section 4 (they reach and take a position) yet comply trivially, because the model never wanted the rejected option — so they inflate n and pull the headline toward 0 with no evidence the record did any work. False REJECTION is conservative: it only shrinks n and widens the bound, which TRAP-SPEC already accepts by construction. Under scenario 3 the corpus chose the temptation, so a loose gate was tolerable; under scenario 4 the AUTHOR chooses it, and section 3 commits to answering that threat by mechanism rather than intention. Measured operating characteristics: 4/2-of admits a p=0.25 constraint 26.2% of the time, and under a 40% weak-authoring bias 16.0% of the admitted set would be weak. 6/4-of cuts admission at p=0.25 to 3.8% and the weak fraction to 3.3%. 3-of-4 reaches a comparable 5.1% at no extra cell cost but rejects 52.5% of genuinely tempting p=0.60 constraints, spending the scarce input (authoring) to save the abundant one (money). The 2 extra cells are not overhead: P is a real arm of the ladder, so k=6 also tightens the P-cell baseline. Cost is +50% on the floor, about $3,961 for 50 constraints at the ruled 40% repo cap. No retroactive confound: the floor has never been run for any trap, the 5 anchor constraints included, so both sets are gated at 6/4-of from scratch and the section 5 comparison stays clean. Tightening is what standing constraint D3 permits.
- 2026-08-10T08:01:42.078Z — rule: **Never let one repo supply more than 40% of scenario 4's primary denominator, and never run with fewer than 3 repos contributing; publish per-repo n beside the headline every time.** — chose **Add a per-repo concentration cap to scenario 4: no single repo may contribute more than 40% of the primary denominator, and at least 3 repos must contribute. Per-repo n is published next to the headline alongside distinct-constraint count. Ruled by the run owner 2026-08-10.** over Leaving concentration to TRAP-SPEC 2.8's existing 10% per-constraint cap; weighting the set toward brillo on fidelity grounds and paying the higher cost; allocating purely for cost with concentration disclosed only in the caveats log. because The pre-registration's open item asked which cap binds first and the answer is that NEITHER did — the 10% per-constraint cap is slack at this set size and there was no per-repo cap at all. At 45-60 constraints, ~1.5 ruled variants x 3 arms gives ~3 sprung sessions per constraint against a denominator of ~150, i.e. 2.0% — the 10% cap cannot bind until the set falls below ~15 constraints. So the real concentration exposure was per-repo and entirely ungoverned. It matters here because the four candidate hosts are deeply unequal: brillo (41 initiatives, 264 decisions, 49 native standing constraints) and sofar (34 / 228 / 30) have a native rule corpus; sofar-cloud (5 / 134 / 0) and algrowth (3 / 43 / 0) have never carried a single standing constraint. Cost runs the other way — $7.14 per P session in algrowth against $23.98 in brillo, a 3.4x spread that tracks repo weight (M5) — so an uncapped cost-minimising allocation lands the claim in exactly the two repos where a planted rule is least in-distribution and where supply is thinnest (25 constraints across algrowth's 3 initiatives would be ~8 planted rules each, above the historical q3 of 5). 40% with a 3-repo minimum stops any one repo carrying the claim while still permitting a cost tilt: ~$3,961 at the ruled k=6, against $5,275 brillo-heavy and $3,759 uncapped. The lone-planted-rule worry is separately dead and needs no cap: 10 of the 21 rule-carrying initiatives hold exactly one standing constraint, so a single planted rule is the modal historical case, not a conspicuous one.
- 2026-08-10T08:01:56.324Z — rule: **Match every authored field's word count into the reference IQR and claim phrasing fidelity only when the blind discrimination test's 95% CI upper bound on grader accuracy is below 0.65 — publish the measured accuracy either way.** — chose **Settle section 2.5 phrasing-match as a two-part procedure with a pre-registered equivalence bound: (1) mechanical band-match — every authored field's word count must fall inside the reference IQR; (2) a blind discrimination test on ~50 authored plus ~50 historical decision entries, decision text only, comparators drawn from the same repos. Fidelity is claimed ONLY if the 95% CI upper bound on pooled grader accuracy falls below 0.65; the measured accuracy is published whichever way it falls. Ruled by the run owner 2026-08-10.** over Band-matching only with grader accuracy reported as an unbounded finding; or a stricter CI upper bound of 0.60. because Length-matching alone is the weakest possible fidelity claim — length is the easiest feature to match and the least likely to be what a grader actually discriminates on — so the discrimination test is what carries the claim and the band-match is only its floor. The bound must be pre-registered as an equivalence bound rather than reported as 'graders were at chance', which is accepting the null: an underpowered test would then be rewarded for being uninformative. 0.65 is the tightest bar ~100 items can honestly support, since the 95% CI halfwidth there is about 10pp; 0.60 would require point accuracy at essentially exactly 0.50, making the test a coin flip on itself and needing 200+ items to be fair. Reference bands measured from the 471 eligible historical decisions (word counts, q1/med/q3): chose 24/36/56, over 13/20/31, because 50/80/120. The rule field is the exposed one and its limitation is stated rather than hidden: only 62 usable ruled decisions exist across the four live records (79 less the 17 in drift-certification and drift-hardening, which S4 excludes), they come from just 2 repos — brillo 49 and sofar 30 — and their band is q1 26 / med 30 / q3 36 words. So rule-voice fidelity for constraints planted in sofar-cloud or algrowth is necessarily borrowed from repos other than the host, and that is a caveat the report carries, not a gap the procedure can close.
